questions.a: Stars are burning balls of gas; constellations are groups of stars forming patterns, like the Big Dipper (Saptarshi).
Saptarshi (Big Dipper/Ursa Major) - seven bright stars like a ladle.

questions.q: Why do stars look tiny though they are huge?
questions.a: They are unimaginably far away, so their light reaches us from tiny points.

questions.q: What is best for watching the night sky?
questions.a: A dark, open place away from city lights; binoculars or a telescope help.

questions.q: Name two objects visible in the night sky without a telescope.
questions.a: The moon and bright planets like Venus (and stars).

questions.q: Why do stars seem to twinkle?
questions.a: Their light bends through moving layers of air, changing brightness.

questions.q: Name the members of our solar system.
questions.a: The sun, eight planets, their moons, asteroids and comets.

questions.q: Which is the largest planet of the solar system?
questions.a: Jupiter - a giant ball of gas with many moons.

questions.q: Why does the sun look bigger than other stars?
questions.a: It is the nearest star to us; other stars are light-years away.

concepts.title: The Milky Way and the Universe

questions.a: Our galaxy - a huge wheel of billions of stars including our sun, seen as a milky band at night.

questions.q: How far is the sun from us compared to other stars?
questions.a: Nearest - about 150 million km; other stars are trillions of times farther.
The distance light travels in one year - used to measure vast space distances.
